title: Three-rune shift display: recovery control
question: Does a locally ranked three-rune shift display recover known decoded pages strongly enough to justify a later LP2 screen?
reader_question: If fragments look like English, did the method recover the page?
summary: The highest-scoring displayed row beat all 49 shuffled searches but recovered only 129 of 207 known runes. The recovery gate failed; no unsolved LP2 page was screened.
finding: Across 51 known-page/start displays, the source's first-ranked rows recovered an average 50.4% of rune positions. The added English scorer selected an LP1-06 row with 129/207=62.3% exact runes; no one of 49 full-search shuffle maxima scored as high, yet the declared 70% recovery gate failed.
limitations: The original program ranks three-rune blocks independently and does not define a coherent decoder or English acceptance gate. Its language-model training overlap with the known readings is not excluded. The +7 plant tests a simple fixed shift, and 49 shuffles are a finite display control, not a cipher null or a probability claim.
next_steps: Require a rule connecting blocks, then demonstrate known-reading recovery and a matched complete-search control before testing unsolved pages.

scope.representation: 17 already decoded GP29 rune streams, 15 from LP1 and the two solved LP2 end pages, each shifted by +7 modulo 29.
scope.procedure: Execute pinned NGramShifter on each page at three starting positions, preserving all 29 ranked local shifts per block; score complete printed rows and compare with 49 shared within-page shuffles.
scope.parameters: 51 page/start displays; 29 rank rows each; 100 scored quadgram eligibility; selected recovery >=70% and score above >=47/49 shuffle maxima required before any target screen.
scope.exclusions: No unsolved LP2 target, global key constraint, interrupted cipher, validation of unknown key laws, or held-out language-model claim.

review.reviewer: Exact pinned source output and independent modular enumeration; complete 49-search selection recheck

reproduction.command: python -X utf8 experiments/records/relikd-trigram-shift-control/run.py --source-root PATH_TO_PINNED_LIBERPRAYGROUND --check && python experiments/records/relikd-trigram-shift-control/check.py --source-root PATH_TO_PINNED_LIBERPRAYGROUND && python experiments/records/relikd-trigram-shift-control/plot.py --check
reproduction.environment: Python 3 standard library and a separate Git checkout at revision 719380ebee0523ad7f2fbf389c6f960d51bea5a4; unlicensed original code is read as verified Git blobs, not bundled. Python -X utf8 handles its implicit source-file decoding on Windows.

visuals.caption: High English score and incomplete known-text recovery in the same selected row.

reader_finding: The highest-scoring row still had 78 wrong runes out of 207. The tool found some correct fragments, but did not recover the known page well enough for the planned LP2 test.
reader_limit: Only known readings were tested; the scorer's training overlap is unknown.
